awd_titl_txt: Conference: US Participation in Frontiers in Harmonic Analysis, Elliptic and Parabolic PDEs, and GMT at the Isaac Newton Institute for the Mathematical Sciences
awd_abstract_narration:
This award will support participation by US-based researchers in the semester-long international research program, “Frontiers in harmonic analysis, elliptic and parabolic PDEs, and GMT,” to be held at the Isaac Newton Institute for Mathematical Sciences, Cambridge, United Kingdom, January 6 to April 30, 2027.  The award will provide support to facilitate long-term research visits as well as shorter visits for three program workshops by US-based researchers.  The program focuses on three research areas, harmonic analysis, elliptic and parabolic partial differential equations, and geometric measure theory, which are deeply and historically linked to one another and to applications in physical and information systems.  The past several years have seen astounding progress in these areas, with new human insights and technological capabilities suggesting the potential for rapid progress in the coming years.  The program seeks to capitalize on these developments, and this award to ensure the ability of US-based researchers to participate fully.  

Research on the areas of focus in the program has developed along two themes:  Theme A:  Fourier analysis and fractal and incidence geometry; and Theme B:  Minimal regularity partial differential equations and operators, and uniform rectifiability. These themes are deeply intertwined, from their foundations to modern approaches, and both feature a rich interplay between geometric intuition and hard analytic estimates.  At the same time, two somewhat separate communities have developed.  The goal of this program is to bring together researchers from both themes to capitalize on recent parallel bursts of activity in both areas to help build mathematical connections and facilitate new developments and collaborations involving researchers from around the world.  Program website:  https://www.newton.ac.uk/event/fha/

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.
